purpose: Lusutrombopag is used to raise your platelet count if it is too low before you have a medical procedure. Low platelets can increase your risk of bleeding, and this medicine helps reduce that risk. It is specifically used in adults with chronic liver disease who need a procedure done.
how_it_works: Your body makes platelets using a natural substance called thrombopoietin. Lusutrombopag works by mimicking this substance and attaching to the same spot on your bone marrow cells, telling them to make more platelets. Think of it like pressing a button that tells your body to produce more of these important clotting cells.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is headache. Some people may also experience nausea or feel generally unwell. Most side effects are mild, but let your doctor or pharmacist know if anything bothers you.
warnings: This medicine can increase your risk of blood clots, which can be serious. Tell your doctor right away if you notice swelling, pain, redness in your leg, chest pain, or sudden shortness of breath. Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding without talking to your doctor first, as it may harm your baby.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 3 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day for 7 days. You typically start taking it about 8 to 14 days before your scheduled procedure. Take it at the same time each day, with or without food.
